American restaurants, unlike Chinese ones, use broccoli, onion, and dairy products in their recipes. Finally, fortune cookies, so popular in the U.S., are an American invention not generally available in China.

contents.text: A biological toilet, or composting toilet, isn't hooked up to sewer lines. The unit has a seat and a lid, but not a toilet bowl filled with water. How does it function? First, the waste is deposited into the unit in the normal way. After that, natural processes take over: ninety percent of the waste is water, which evaporates into the air. The toilet usually has fans and ventilation to assist in this process. The solid part of the waste then remains in a chamber, where it decomposes. Specialized bacteria digest the waste, given the right combination of oxygen, moisture, and heat. When the decomposition process is complete, the compost from the toilet can be removed and used in gardens and around trees.

Recent research has revealed how people living 13,000 feet above sea level in the mountains of Tibet have adapted to their oxygen-poor environment. The Tibetan population, as a consequence of living at high altitude for thousands of years, has developed several characteristics that allow them to survive and thrive in this type of environment. header.text: A restrictive element in a sentence is necessary in order for a reader to identify exactly who or what is being discussed. Restrictive information is not set off with commas.

sentences.text: The teacher <u>who is retiring</u> is being honored with an award on Friday.

The teacher is being honored with an award on Friday.
Without the restrictive clause, a reader doesn't know which teacher is being honored.

header.text: A nonrestrictive element provides information that is supplemental; it is not necessary in order for a reader to identify who or what is being discussed. Nonrestrictive information is always set off with commas.

sentences.text: The Golden Gate Bridge, <u>which first opened in 1937</u>, took over four years to build.
The underlined information isn't required to interpret the sentence.
The Golden Gate Bridge took over four years to build.
Without the information, a reader still knows which bridge took four years to build.
